stories.title: DRC to move its embassy in 'Israel' to Jerusalem
stories.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo plans to relocate its embassy in 'Israel' from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. The move would make the DRC one of a small number of countries with diplomatic missions in Jerusalem, whose status remains disputed. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) plans to move its embassy in 'Israel' from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, according to a joint statement issued by the two countries. The announcement came during DRC President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi's state visit to 'Israel', where he met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Isaac Herzog. The two sides said they would take steps to relocate the diplomatic mission to Jerusalem, without providing a specific timeline. The move is politically sensitive because the status of Jerusalem remains one of the core issues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. 'Israel' claims Jerusalem as its capital, while the Palestinian Authority seeks occupied East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Most countries have historically maintained their embassies in the Tel Aviv area to avoid taking a position on Jerusalem's disputed status and to preserve room for future peace negotiations. The US, Guatemala, Honduras, Kosovo, Papua New Guinea, Paraguay, Fiji and Somaliland currently have embassies in Jerusalem. Colombia and the Pacific island nation of Nauru have also announced plans in recent months to establish diplomatic missions in the city. If implemented, the DRC's move would bring the number of embassies in Jerusalem to 11.

stories.title: KV7 channel activation inhibits human and murine myometrium contractility and delays delivery in a mouse model of preterm birth
stories.description: Spontaneous preterm birth, defined as delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, remains a global cause of neonatal illness and death, yet treatments for preterm labor remain limited. We hypothesized that KV7 channels in the uterus (myometrium), could be a therapeutic target for preventing or treating preterm labor. The aim was to characterize KV7 channel subtypes in human myometrium present after labor onset, and to use a preterm birth mouse model to provide proof-of-principal evidence that activating these channels in vivo can delay preterm delivery. This experimental study integrated studies of human myometrial tissue (term and preterm pregnancies, n = 159 across experiments), with a RU486-induced preterm birth mouse model (C57BL/6 J, n = 6-9 per experimental group), and ex vivo fetal ductus arteriosus preparations (CD-1 mice, n = 10 per group). Molecular and protein profiling, isometric tension recordings, and functional pharmacology were used to characterize KV7 mediated regulation of human and mouse uterine contractility. In vivo dosing studies in mice assessed the effects of KV7 activators (retigabine and ML213) on delivery timing (n = 6-9). We show that KV7 channels and ancillary units (KCNE1-5), are expressed in pregnant human myometrium, prior to and after the onset of labor. KCNQ4 and KCNE4 transcripts are also present in myometrium taken at preterm gestations ( ± labor). KV7.2-5 activators markedly reduce spontaneous contractions in human and mouse myometrium in vitro and significantly delay preterm birth in vivo with limited impact on fetal ductus arteriosus function. These findings support KV7 activation as a promising approach to suppress uterine contractility and hence delay preterm birth, highlighting a potential new direction for either drug repurposing or therapeutic development. Preterm birth, when a baby is born before 37 weeks of pregnancy, is a major cause of illness and death in newborns. Unfortunately, there are few effective treatments to delay early labor. This study explores whether a group of proteins called KV7 channels, found in the muscle of the uterus (womb), could be targeted to prevent preterm labor. We examined human uterine tissue from term and preterm pregnancies and used a mouse model of preterm birth to test drugs that activate KV7 channels. We found these channels are present and functional in labor and that activating them reduces uterine contractions and delays preterm birth in mice. This suggests KV7 targeting drugs could offer a new approach to preventing preterm labor in the future. Mansour, Mistry et al. perform integrated experiments on pregnant human myometrial tissue and a preterm birth mouse model to examine whether activating uterine KV7 channels can delay preterm labor. They report that KV7 channels persist in laboring human myometrium and that KV7.2-5 activators suppress contractions and delay preterm birth in mice.

stories.title: LDA-YOLO11: a lightweight detail-attention detector for edge-deployable road surface defect detection
stories.description: Road surface defects, such as cracks, pavement damage and potholes, shorten road service life and affect driving safety and preventive maintenance. Existing lightweight object detectors are computationally efficient but still suffer from missed detections and unstable localization when dealing with elongated cracks, weak-texture damage and complex pavement backgrounds. To address these issues, this study proposes LDA-YOLO11, a lightweight detail-attention road defect detector based on YOLO11n. The model improves the neck feature fusion stage while keeping the original YOLO11n backbone and $$P_3^{\prime }$$, $$P_4$$ and $$P_5$$ detection heads unchanged. A $$P_2$$-guided Detail-Neck is designed to inject shallow high-resolution detail information into the $$P_3^{\prime }$$ feature without adding an independent $$P_2$$ detection head. Efficient Channel Attention modules are further introduced after the final $$P_3^{\prime }$$ and $$P_4$$ fusion features to recalibrate defect-related channel responses and suppress background interference. Experimental results show that LDA-YOLO11 achieves mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 values of 0.951 and 0.791, improving YOLO11n by 2.3 and 1.7% points, respectively. On the Jetson Orin NX platform, TensorRT FP16 acceleration reduces the inference latency to 27 ms/image, corresponding to 37.03 FPS, while causing only a 0.2%-point decrease in mAP@0.5. These results indicate that LDA-YOLO11 demonstrates promising edge deployment feasibility and real-time inference capability for road surface defect detection.

stories.title: Coupling effects of nano-silica and steel fibers on concrete performance and microstructural characterization
stories.description: The present investigation examines the coupled effects of steel fibre reinforcement and nano-silica (NS) addition on the permeability and mechanical properties of concrete. End-hooked steel fibres (designated as D) and sheared crimped steel fibres (designated as B) of varying lengths were first incorporated into concrete mixtures to evaluate their influence on water permeability, with the objective of identifying the fibre geometry and size that yield optimal impermeability. Experimental results demonstrated that the inclusion of either fibre type effectively enhanced the resistance to water penetration; among all tested variants, D50 (end-hooked steel fibres of 50 mm length) and B40 (sheared crimped steel fibres of 40 mm length) exhibited the most pronounced improvements, corresponding to a 33.33% and 25% reduction in permeability, respectively, relative to the plain concrete(PC) without fibres. Subsequently, D50 and B40 fibres were combined with NS at various dosages to investigate the coupling effect of fibre and NS addition on the mechanical behaviour of concrete. An orthogonal experimental design was adopted, with fibre contents of 1%, 1.5% and 2% by volume, and NS contents of 0.5%, 1% and 1.5% by mass of cementitious materials. The results indicated that the most significant enhancement in mechanical performance was achieved at 2% fibre content and 1% NS content. Under these optimal proportions, end-hooked steel fibre-reinforced concrete (E-S) exhibited a compressive strength improvement comparable to that of sheared crimped steel fibre-reinforced concrete (S-W); however, the splitting tensile strength and bending strength of E-S were considerably superior to those of S-W. The underlying mechanism governing the coupled effect of steel fibres and NS on concrete performance was further elucidated through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analyses from a microstructural perspective. The findings provide a solid theoretical basis for understanding the combined influence of fibre reinforcement and nanoparticle incorporation on both the impermeability and mechanical response of concrete.
